title: Starvation and Washing Protocol for Anaerobic Ciliates
author: Roxanne Beinart
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.868hzhw

steps.title: Pick and Initial Wash of Ciliate Cells
steps.instruction: Isolate live ciliate cells and perform an initial cleaning process using filtered media.

substeps.instruction: Use a sterile drawn glass Pasteur pipette, a sterile depression slide with multiple wells, and an inverted microscope to transfer several hundred live cells into clean media (0.22 μm filtered).
Pass the cells through 3 wells of 0.22 μm filtered clean media.

steps.title: Transfer Cells to Hypoxic Media
steps.instruction: Transfer healthy and active cells into a sterile environment for starvation.

substeps.instruction: Pass the remaining healthy looking and active cells into a sterile 1.5 ml eppendorf tube containing 0.5 ml of clean, 0.22 μm filtered and hypoxic media.

steps.title: Starve Ciliate Cells
steps.instruction: Allow cells to starve while monitoring their condition and the media for contamination.

substeps.instruction: Let the cells starve for 4 - 12 hours, adapted to the specific ciliate taxa based on oxygen tolerance, general endurance, and sensitivity to other conditions.

Every hour, isolate one cell using a clean glass micropipette, place it on a microscope slide, and observe under a light microscope to check for the presence of full food vacuoles and overall health; adjust starvation time accordingly.
End starvation and proceed to washing once a sufficient number of cells lack food vacuoles and no bacterial growth is present in the media.

steps.title: Handle Bacterial Contamination
steps.instruction: If bacterial growth appears during starvation, perform a rescue wash.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the cells into clean filtered media.
Place cells into a new eppendorf tube with clean filtered hypoxic media.

steps.title: Wash Starved Cells
steps.instruction: Clean the starved cells using sterile hypoxic filtered media.

substeps.instruction: Carefully wash starved cells in a drop of sterile hypoxic filtered media.
Transfer cells through four to six drops of sterile hypoxic filtered media; reduce the number of washings if cells tend to burst, or increase if free-living prokaryotes are visible.

steps.title: Prepare Cells for DNA Isolation
steps.instruction: Preserve the cleaned starved cells in a stabilization buffer.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 50 - 100 cleaned starved cells into a sterile eppendorf tube with 200 μl of DNA Shield product (Zymo Research).
